coverage_note: Amal's voice is missing 00:00-23:14 (only her CHAT lines), so early fixes are judged from chat and Medi's echoes; 02:49 الساعة واحد was self-fixed at 02:55 before any chat, not written. 09:46-14:13 is an English phone call. 49:00-1:01:00 is in Latin letters (awal/oola/nafs drill). Much of 29:00-1:04:00 is rule discussion and questions, not counted. شيء is on her sheet (Kul shee, Wala shee) so not flagged. 04:02 شوك = engine for شوب (sheet: El-jaw shoab), not flagged. Names: Amal, Male (place).

rows.medi_said: الساعة واحدة و، uh، صباح. ... ثمان دقايق
rows.right: el-sube7 (الصبح) - or drop it, as her chat did
rows.why: He used صباح (as in 'good morning') for 'in the morning'; her sheet has morning | el-sube7 | الصبح, and her chat silently dropped the word (my reading).
He used مشجع (encouraging/encourager) for 'motivated'; she typed mitshajje3 = motivated - wrong form of a root he knows.
'Motivated for the lesson' needs a preposition (la-) before الدرس; he put the noun straight after the adjective and no fix was voiced (my reading).

rows.medi_said: أنا في الـ Wi-Fi? Is that how you say it? ... So أنا على الـ Wi-Fi?
rows.why: He used في for 'on the Wi-Fi'; Amal's voice is missing here but he immediately echoes على as her answer (14:37-14:51).

rows.medi_said: so it's not إلي? الـ BMW إلي؟
rows.why: He tried to possess the brand name directly (الـ BMW إلي); her chat gives sayyaaret el-BM illi - the thing (car) first, then the owner.

rows.medi_said: So Shanteti, ... Would it be El Shogol?
rows.amal_said: Yes, but what's work bag without any my or yours?
rows.why: He put the possessive ending on the first word of the idafa (Shanteti); Amal prompted 'work bag without any my' and he fixed to 'Shantet Shogoli, not Shanteti Shogoli'; she said صح.

rows.medi_said: So Shantet Shogoli, uh, uh, Amra.
rows.amal_said: That would mean is red.
rows.why: An adjective after a definite (possessed) noun needs el-; without it Amal says it means 'is red' and explains the adjective must be definite too.

rows.medi_said: So would it be شنتت، شنتت شغلي الأحمر، الأحمر،
rows.amal_said: الحمرا.
rows.why: شنتة is feminine so the adjective is الحمرا; Amal recast at once and he repeated الحمراء.

rows.medi_said: شنتت شغلي، اه، الحمراء، اه، ما فيهون.
rows.amal_said: Not here. ... ما فيهن means there aren't here or there isn't here.
rows.why: He negated 'here' with ما فيهون; Amal said that means 'there isn't (any) here', he tried مش هون and she confirmed (مشون), chat mish hon.
rows.english: My red work bag is not here.

rows.amal_said: ليش؟ لا، ليش. ... It's just اسم. Why would it be feminine?
rows.why: He gave masculine اسم a feminine -t before the owner (اسميت); Amal said لا and that اسم can't be feminine.
rows.english: The name of his old school.

rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm.
rows.why: A noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; the engine shows الـ before مدرسته and Amal only said Mm-hmm (could be a filler - low).
rows.english: The name of his old school.

rows.amal_said: لا.
rows.right: اسم (first word of idafa takes no el-)
rows.why: He put el- on اسم, the first word of the idafa; Amal said لا (and again at 30:21 when he asked).
rows.english: The old name of his school.

rows.medi_said: So الـ اسم قديم. No, it's like اسم القديمة. Okay, I don't know.
rows.amal_said: لا. لا. You just change the gender of Adeem.
rows.why: For 'the old name' the adjective must agree with masculine اسم (el-2adeem); he said القديمة and Amal said لا and that only the gender of قديم changes.
rows.english: The old name of his school.

rows.amal_said: But her. Her favorite store.
rows.why: He left out 'her'; Amal prompted 'But her' and he later put -ha on the last noun (محل أواى ها المفضل), chat ma7al awa3iha el-mufaddal.

rows.amal_said: No. Even though in English we don't-- we say the, in Arabic we don't.
rows.why: Superlative أحسن + noun takes no el-; Amal said No and explained, he fixed to أحسن محل.

rows.amal_said: Mm, it works, yeah. هذا أحسن محل is like more efficient.
rows.why: محل is masculine so it takes هذا, not هذي; Amal said it works and recast with هذا without naming the gender slip.

rows.amal_said: The worst.
rows.why: Superlative + noun takes no el- (her rule at 42:49); he said أسوأ الزبون twice and her chat writes aswa2 zboon without el-.

rows.medi_said: Okay. So أحسن الزبون ما، ما تشتري إشي.
rows.why: He was building 'the worst customer' but said أحسن (best); not voiced by Amal, her chat has aswa2 (my reading; may be a slip of the tongue).
rows.english: The worst customer is the one who doesn't buy anything.

rows.amal_said: It's ما بي، ما بيشتري because it's زبون.
rows.why: The subject زبون is masculine so the verb is بيشتري; Amal recast and said 'because it's زبون'.
rows.english: The worst customer is the one who doesn't buy anything.

rows.amal_said: أكثر حدا بحبه.
rows.why: He used هذا (this) for 'person/someone'; Amal repeated أكثر حدا (46:11, 46:20, 46:43); sheet: first person | Awal 7ada.
rows.english: The person I like the most.

rows.amal_said: بحبه.
rows.why: The verb needs the pointer ending back to the person (بحبه); Amal recast and he said 'There's a pointer'.
rows.english: The person I like the most.

rows.amal_said: Why? ... if you say the week's beginning, now you'd have to be إضافة
rows.why: He read الأسبوع الأول (noun + adjective) as an idafa 'the week's beginning'; Amal asked why and explained that would need إضافة; he fixed to 'the first week'.

rows.medi_said: Il awal il tamreen or il tamreen il awal
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. ... Of course.
rows.why: Amal's rule (48:15): أول before the noun never takes el-; his first option breaks it and she let it pass while accepting the second.

rows.amal_said: Al oola. ... Al laffa al oola.
rows.chat: awal laffe, awal el-lafe, el-laffe el-oola
rows.why: He kept repeating her phrase as laffe (il) aula and missed its meaning until she broke it down; she said No to 'laffe il aula doesn't mean anything'.

rows.amal_said: Tani ishi. ... The second thing.
rows.why: He glossed tani ishi as 'something else'; Amal corrected: tani ishi = the second thing, ishi tani = something else (sheet: something else | Eshi taani).

rows.amal_said: Nafs al ishi. ... نفس إشي doesn't mean anything.
rows.why: 'The same thing' is نفس الإشي; Amal recast at once and later said نفس إشي doesn't mean anything (chat nafs el-ishi). No bucket fits exactly; A1 is nearest (el- placement).
